title: Beyond Consensus: Downward Bias and Role Asymmetry in Multi-Agent LLM Judges for Subjective Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2608.30373v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) has been widely adopted to improve LLM-based evaluation by prompting multiple agents to negotiate and reach a consensus. However, for subjective rubric-based scoring, inter-agent agreement does not guarantee alignment with human judgments. In this paper, we compare a single-judge baseline against a consensus-based MAD protocol on subjective evaluation tasks and design three ablations to isolate the impact of role prompting, multi-round interaction, and explicit score sharing. Evaluations across six LLMs show that the single-judge baseline achieves the strongest human alignment on average across six judge models, whereas MAD shows degradation in human alignment on both tasks. translated_title: 超越共识：多智能体LLM评审在主观评估中的向下偏差与角色不对称性
translated_abstract: 多智能体辩论（MAD）已被广泛用于改进基于LLM的评估，其方式是促使多个智能体进行协商并达成共识。然而，对于基于评分标准的主观打分任务，智能体之间的一致性并不能保证与人类判断的对齐。本文在主观评估任务上将单一评审基线与基于共识的MAD协议进行比较，并设计了三个消融实验以分离角色提示、多轮交互和显式分数共享的影响。在六个LLM上的评估表明，单一评审基线在六个评审模型上平均实现了最强的人类对齐，而MAD在两个任务上均表现出人类对齐的下降。我们的消融实验证明，这一性能下降主要源于不对称的角色提示，而非交互本身。具体而言，赋予严格评审角色会引入一种系统性的向下偏差，而共识过程……
tldr: 研究发现多智能体辩论（MAD）在主观评估中反而降低与人类判断的对齐度，其性能下降主要源于不对称的角色提示——尤其是严格评审角色引入的系统性向下偏差——而非多轮交互本身。
en_tdlr: Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) degrades human alignment in subjective LLM-based evaluation, and this performance drop stems primarily from asymmetric role prompting—particularly the systematic downward bias introduced by strict judge roles—rather than from the multi-round interaction itself.
